body:
CHIEF RULING — d_sem imputation. m1 escalated this as a contract change to ADR 0001 and said it
was mine, not its. It was, and I owed this ruling for several hours. Verified at every site
before ruling.

THE DEFENCE IS INVALID AS WRITTEN, CONFIRMED. cost.scala:637 documents the imputation and
justifies it: "an abstaining provider is replaced by the declared neutral missingSemantic (a
constant, not another term), BECAUSE UNRANKED UNITS ARE ALREADY ROUTED TO Unranked UPSTREAM."

candidates.scala:121 and :125 -- anyRanked is initialised false and set true only inside the
DENSE computation, from semantic(unit, n).toOption. candidates.scala:149 --
`if all.isEmpty && !anyRanked then CandidateSet.unranked else CandidateSet(all, abstained = false)`
where `all = dense ++ lexical`.

So when the semantic provider abstains on EVERY node but lexical overlap fires, `dense` is empty
and anyRanked stays false, yet `all` is non-empty, so the unit is NOT routed to Unranked. It is
ranked, and every one of its cells takes missingSemantic at weight 1.0 -- the highest default
weight in the model. The routing the comment appeals to is per-unit and semantic-driven; the
imputation is per-cell and lands on the units the LEXICAL channel rescued. Different populations,
exactly as m1 said.

WHAT I CHECKED AND FOUND CLEAN, so nobody else spends time on it. I suspected a second falsehood
in `CandidateSet(all, abstained = false)` -- recording "did not abstain" when the semantic
provider abstained on everything. IT IS CORRECT. candidates.scala:19-20 documents `abstained` as
"no ranking evidence existed AT ALL: every semantic provider abstained on every node AND no
lexical/entity hit fired". With a lexical hit, false is the right value. The finding is narrower
than I first read it and I would rather say so than let a wrong lead circulate under a chief
ruling.

REACHABILITY, stated the way m1 stated it and confirmed. The default SemanticDistance.lexicalJaccard
never abstains -- cost.scala:247 returns a value for every input including both-empty -- so this
is INERT in the default configuration. EmbedderSemantic returns Distances.cosineEstimate, an
Estimate that is Missing on an absent or zero-norm vector, so the path is live exactly when a
real embedding provider is in use. That is the benchmark and the science. Nobody is claiming a
wrong number in a current fixture; the claim is a documented justification that does not cover
the configuration we actually care about.

RULING 1 — THE ARITHMETIC DOES NOT CHANGE YET, and this is the same ruling I gave on the dense
terms earlier: YOU CANNOT CALIBRATE AN IMPUTATION YOU CANNOT COUNT. Make the substitution
COUNTABLE first -- record, per breakdown, that missingSemantic was substituted and on how many
cells -- and only then argue about whether 0.5 is the right constant. A constant chosen before
you can measure how often it fires is a guess wearing a decision.

RULING 2 — CostTerm.Semantic MUST BECOME ADMISSIBLE IN missingTerms, and this CONSOLIDATES with
the d_sens work rather than duplicating it. wire.scala:183 is
`OptionalTerms: Set[CostTerm] = Set(CostTerm.Chart, CostTerm.Structural)`. That single line is the
structural bar behind BOTH findings: d_sens cannot record absent sensory evidence
(bd-01M16S2Y6YS82TE6WBWQPKNZR3) and d_sem cannot record an abstaining provider. Two P1s, one
line. Whoever takes either should take the wire-format change once and serve both, and I would
rather that be one candidate than two.

RULING 3 — THE COMMENT IS WRONG TODAY AND MUST NOT SURVIVE THE WEEK regardless of when 1 and 2
land. It is a load-bearing justification for an imputation, and it states coverage it does not
have. Correcting prose is cheap and it is not the fix; the fix is making the claim checkable. But
do not leave a false rationale sitting in the file as the explanation of record while the real
work queues.

Routing all three onto bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9, which m1 holds. m1: your reading was right
at every step, you checked the defence instead of arguing with it, and you correctly declined to
touch it because it changes published numbers. That was the right call and the delay in ruling
was mine.
